title: Most phyllotaxis has between two and three leaves per turn of the genetic spiral

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Most phyllotaxis has between two and three leaves per turn of the genetic spiral

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The prevalence of Fibonacci parastichy numbers arises because in the great majority of fir-cones and other phyllotactic systems there are more than two but fewer than three leaves in one turn of the genetic spiral (t = 2); other observed series correspond to t = 3, 4, 5.

fields.label: Notation
fields.value: t = 2 (more than two, fewer than three leaves per turn of the genetic spiral) \Rightarrow parastichy pairs from 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, \dots; t = 3, 4, 5 give other series

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. XIV: On Leaf-Arrangement, or Phyllotaxis

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: And, determined in this manner, it is found in the great majority of cases, in fir-cones and a host of other examples of phyllotaxis, that _t_ = 2.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter XIV, “On Leaf-Arrangement, or Phyllotaxis”; topic “Tait's explanation of the numbers”. Scope: spiral phyllotaxis in plants

fields.label: Notation
fields.value: t = 2 (more than two, fewer than three leaves per turn of the genetic spiral) \Rightarrow parastichy pairs from 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, \dots; t = 3, 4, 5 give other series

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch14-08: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.70

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The numerical prevalence claim is measurable, but genetic-spiral reconstruction requires high-quality organ maps. Current data can test fir-cones and selected taxa, not confidently the claimed host of systems.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Infer the number of organs per turn of the genetic spiral from indexed cone and inflorescence images and estimate the fraction lying between two and three, along with frequencies corresponding to t = 3, 4 and 5. A clear majority in the stated interval supports the claim; another interval dominating refutes it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Available imagery is not representative of all phyllotactic systems.

The genetic order is often not recoverable from a single mature image.

fields.value:

operationalizability: 0.86

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The index t is recoverable from the parastichy pairs Thompson treats as ordinary observations, so the frequency claim is empirically sharp. The deposited counts that make the conversion easy are mostly sunflowers, which are a poor sample of 'the great majority' of cones and leafy shoots. Published cone surveys fill some of the gap only after compilation, so the global prevalence statement is only partly testable now.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Infer the leaves-per-turn index t from parastichy pairs or divergence angles across cones and other shoots, and estimate the fraction of systems with 2 < t < 3. The prevalence claim is supported if that class dominates and the other observed series sit at t = 3, 4, or 5; a large share of systems outside those bins would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Sunflower heads are a high-Fibonacci subset and will overstate the share of systems near the golden angle.

No open catalogue records t, or even parastichy pairs, across the vascular plants.

data existence: 0.55
discriminating power: 0.7
operationalizability: 0.8
